topics.definition: A Database Management System (DBMS) is software used to create, store, retrieve and manage data efficiently.
DBMS provides efficient data storage, security, consistency and sharing.
topics.example: Multiple users can access the same database.

topics.definition: A DBMS supports data independence, integrity, concurrency and security.
DBMS architecture can be one-tier, two-tier or three-tier.
tips: Three-tier architecture is common in web applications.

topics.definition: Users include DBA, application programmers, developers and end users.
Data models describe how data is stored and organized.
tips: The relational model is the most widely used.

topics.definition: Schema is the logical structure or blueprint of a database.
An instance is the data stored in the database at a particular moment.
DBMS provides centralized management, while a file system stores data in separate files.
topics.example: DBMS supports SQL; file systems do not.
tips: DBMS offers better security and consistency.

topics.definition: DBMS is used in banking, hospitals, colleges, e-commerce and social media.
tips: Almost every modern application uses a database.
